card.statement:
The (specialized) quantum $D$ -module for the conical Hamiltonian symplectic resolution $X$ is the graded left $R_{Kah,reg}$ -module

(2.15)

$M_{Kah,reg}:=\Lambda\otimes H^{*}_{T\times\mathbb{G}_{m}}(X)\cong k[z^{\alpha},(1-z^{\alpha})^{-1}]\otimes H^{*}_{T\times\mathbb{G}_{m}}(X),$

where the actions of $z^{\alpha}\otimes 1,1\otimes x\in k[z^{\alpha}]\otimes H^{2}_{T\times\mathbb{G}_{m}}(X)\subseteq R_{Kah}$ are given by

(2.16)

$(z^{\alpha}\otimes 1)\cdot(z^{\beta}\otimes y)=z^{\alpha+\beta}\otimes y,\quad(1\otimes x)\cdot(z^{\beta}\otimes y)=(z^{\beta}\otimes 1)(x\star y+1\otimes\hbar\langle\beta,\bar{x}\rangle y)$

Here $\star$ denotes the equivariant quantum product. The action on $(1-z^{\alpha})^{-1}\otimes 1$ is determined as one would define formally for $(1-z)^{-1}=1+z+z^{2}+\cdots$.

Note that the quantum $D$ -module only exists as a $R_{Kah,reg}$ -module, as the quantum product $\star$ involves denominators of the form $(1-z^{\alpha})^{-1}$ for $\alpha\in\Sigma_{Kah,+}$, see 2.20. The quantum $D$ -module is closely related to the object known as the quantum connection, where the action of $x$ is interpreted as the “covariant derivative” $\hbar\partial_{\bar{x}}+x\star$ where $\partial_{\bar{x}}$ acts on the variable $z^{\beta}$ by $\partial_{\bar{x}}z^{\beta}=\langle\beta,\bar{x}\rangle z^{\beta}$.
card.label: Definition 2.27

paper.title: 3D mirror symmetry in positive characteristic
paper.abstract: Via the formulation of (quantum) Hikita conjecture with coefficients in a characteristic $p$ field, we explain an arithmetic aspect of the theory of 3D mirror symmetry. Namely, we propose that the action of Steenrod-type operations and Frobenius-constant quantizations intertwine under the (quantum) Hikita isomorphism for 3D mirror pairs, and verify this for the Springer resolutions and hypertoric varieties.
